title: HST Quick Method: Save Time and Possibly Money on Your HST Returns
excerpt: Most Ontario businesses registered for HST collect 13% and remit the difference after input tax credits. The Quick Method lets you remit a flat percentage of your gross sales instead — saving bookkeeping time and sometimes real money.

title: CRA Installment Payments: Who Owes Them and How to Calculate
excerpt: If your net tax owing exceeded $3,000 in either of the past two years, the CRA requires quarterly installment payments. Missing them costs you interest — even if you pay in full at year-end. Here is how to handle them correctly.

title: RRSP vs TFSA for Self-Employed Canadians: Which Comes First?
excerpt: For employees, the RRSP vs TFSA question has a standard answer. For self-employed Canadians whose income swings year to year, the optimal strategy is more nuanced — and potentially worth thousands more in lifetime tax savings.

title: Ontario Employer Health Tax: Exemptions, Rates, and Filing for Small Business
excerpt: Most Ontario employers pay the Employer Health Tax (EHT) on total payroll — but many small businesses qualify for an exemption on the first $1,000,000 of remuneration. Here is how to calculate your EHT and whether you qualify.

title: HST Registration for New Ontario Businesses: What You Need to Know
excerpt: HST registration is mandatory once you hit $30,000 in revenue — but voluntarily registering earlier can actually save you money. Here is everything a new Ontario business needs to know.

title: Incorporating Your ABA Practice in Ontario: What Behaviour Analysts Need to Know
excerpt: Running an ABA therapy practice as a sole proprietor in Ontario leaves significant tax savings on the table. Here is exactly what incorporating means for behaviour analysts — the benefits, the structure, and what Adapt Business Solutions does for ABA owners.

title: HST and ABA Therapy Services in Ontario: What Is Taxable and What Is Not
excerpt: HST on ABA therapy is one of the most misunderstood tax issues for Ontario behaviour analysts. Getting it wrong — either charging HST when you should not, or not charging when you should — creates significant CRA liability. Here is how to get it right.

title: Tax Deductions for Ontario ABA Business Owners: Every Legitimate Claim
excerpt: ABA practice owners have a wide range of legitimate business deductions that most general accountants miss. This guide covers every major expense category specific to the ABA industry — so you never leave money on the table.

title: Payroll for Ontario ABA Practices: BCBAs, RBTs, and Managing OAP Funding
excerpt: Payroll is one of the most operationally complex parts of running an ABA practice in Ontario — especially when you mix employees, contractors, OAP-funded hours, and private pay clients. Here is how to get it right.

title: Ontario Incorporation: Choosing the Right Share Structure from Day One
excerpt: Most online incorporation services create a simple one-class share structure that works for a single owner — but leaves valuable options on the table. Here is what you should actually be thinking about.
